name: Gateway drain window

checks.expected_incident: 503s on in-flight requests while the gateway restarts/reloads
checks.decision: confirm the class signature before touching anything

checks.expected_incident: non-zero and rising over the drain window (up to ~30 min)
checks.decision: distinguish a drain window (bounded, expected) from a wedged gateway

checks.expected_incident: 503 during drain; 200 again once in-flight requests finish
checks.decision: pause-first decision: hold config rollout until health returns 200

evidence.detail: gateway restart doctrine: pause-first under load

recovery_ladder: Stop config changes: batch them instead of trickling under load.
Pause-first under load: hold the rollout until in-flight requests finish.
Announce the expected drain window (up to ~30 min) to dependents before restarting.
Watch drain-503 volume fall to zero, then confirm health endpoint 200 before resuming.
guardrails: Never restart the gateway with in-flight requests still draining from the previous restart.
Never treat drain 503s as a gateway fault — during a drain window they are EXPECTED; distinguish bounded drain from wedged before acting.
Never trickle config changes under load — batch them and pause-first.

evidence_trail.detail: 2026-08-14T02:15Z post-mortem note: hard kill under load left no drain window; all 214 in-flight requests 503'd

2026-09-16T19:05Z post-mortem note: across incidents 3-4 the drain window was observed at 25-30 min; dependents were not warned in advance during incidents 1-3

SIGKILL received during load; 214 in-flight requests terminated with 503
tick spawn failed: upstream returned 503 (gateway restarting)

new work kept being enqueued during the restart; queue drained after recovery, nothing dropped
